title: Exceptions and input validation
subtitle: When users may enter invalid data, give a fallible conversion a clear failure path.
concept: When users may enter invalid data, give a fallible conversion a clear failure path.
intuition: Someone enters two instead of a numeric quantity. Explain the requirement before asking again.
objectives: Find the operation that can fail
Handle the expected failure with try and except

body.title: Find the operation that can fail
body.text: int("3") succeeds, but int("three") raises ValueError: the text is unsuitable for this conversion. Without handling, the program stops there. Identify the error you intend to handle instead of wrapping everything in an indistinct failure case.

body.title: Handle the expected failure with try and except
body.text: The try body attempts the conversion. except ValueError: handles only that exception type. Success skips except; failure skips the remaining try statements and enters except. Handling an exception does not make the failed operation succeed: it provides understandable feedback.

body.title: Conversion does not guarantee validity
body.text: "-2" converts to an integer, but a shopping quantity cannot be negative. After conversion, test count < 0. A function can reject it with raise ValueError("Quantity cannot be negative"). Do not catch every exception indiscriminately, or spelling bugs and file problems may be misreported as quantity errors.

formalDefinition.text: try attempts a fallible operation; except handles a specified exception. raise explicitly rejects invalid input.
conditions: Catch only expected exception types. After conversion, check the allowed range.

derivation.text: The conversion fails, so execution enters the ValueError handler.
Print a clear requirement rather than continuing with a fabricated number.

commonMistakes.claim: Anything convertible to an integer is a valid quantity.
commonMistakes.correction: Conversion checks the representation. Range requirements, such as nonnegativity, need a separate check.

commonMistakes.claim: After an exception is caught, Python automatically supplies a valid number.
commonMistakes.correction: except runs only the handler you wrote. It does not repair the input.

practice.problem: Convert valid text "4" and display it.
Handle the failure to convert "4.5" directly to an integer.
solution: Conversion fails and prints Enter an integer.

practice.problem: Convert -1, then print Cannot be negative.
practice.hint: Check the range after successful conversion.
solution: Conversion succeeds, but the value is not a valid quantity.

practice.problem: Quantity 0 is allowed. What should the program display?
practice.hint: Reject values below 0, not equal to 0.

learningCheck.question: int can convert "-2". Does that make it a valid shopping quantity?
choices: Successful conversion always means valid input
It still needs a negative-value check
except automatically changes negative values to 0
learningCheck.explanation: Conversion checks whether text represents a number. Validation checks whether that number is allowed.
feedback: Successful conversion only shows that the text represents an integer.
Yes. The application requirement needs a separate check.
except does not automatically change input or supply a replacement value.
